- When sentiment is consistently negative (≥ 3 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 2–3 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., -1 → +1), model often overreacts; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 1–2 days post-sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates sharp downward moves (e.g., 30–50% drop) after negative sentiment; add 3–7% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days if sentiment remains negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model often fails to recognize; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for 2–4 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 3–6% for 1–3 days.
- If model forecast is >45 and true outcome drops below 40, apply 5–10% downward correction for 2–5 days unless sentiment is strong positive.
